Definition: Limited verified paired speech and transcript data for supervised adaptation and evaluation
EstablishedEvidence: Survey challenge and corpus evidence show labeled data is necessary but not sufficient
InterpretiveSynthesis: Labeled hours should be framed as one resource condition within a broader reliability problem
ResidualRisk: May sound generic if not tied to validation and benchmark design

Definition: Available speech without reliable transcripts for SSL continued pretraining or adaptation
EstablishedEvidence: SSL and multilingual SSL show unlabeled speech can change the starting point
InterpretiveSynthesis: Unlabeled speech helps only when language domain and validation conditions are handled
ResidualRisk: Unlabeled data quality and provenance may be hidden

Definition: Speech with noisy or indirect labels such as subtitles web captions or crawled transcripts
EstablishedEvidence: Whisper MMS VoxPopuli and heterogeneous-source evidence show scale and source quality interact
InterpretiveSynthesis: Weak supervision expands coverage while moving risk into filtering validation and evaluation
ResidualRisk: Do not treat weak labels as clean labels
WritingUse: Discuss why web-scale supervision does not end low-resource ASR

Definition: Machine-generated transcripts used as training labels after filtering or selection
EstablishedEvidence: Pseudo-labeling can expand supervision but teacher errors and filtering determine value
InterpretiveSynthesis: Pseudo-labels are a supervision source with reliability conditions rather than free labeled data
ResidualRisk: Teacher quality and confidence thresholds are not comparable across studies

Definition: Cross-language corpora and benchmarks used for transfer evaluation and language coverage
EstablishedEvidence: Common Voice MLS VoxPopuli FLEURS XTREME-S and ML-SUPERB improve coverage
InterpretiveSynthesis: Multilingual coverage must be interpreted through balance metadata and benchmark design
ResidualRisk: Language presence can hide dialect or domain absence

Definition: Speech paired with video visual speech cues or multimodal speech-text tasks
EstablishedEvidence: AVSR and speech-text foundation sources show multimodal promise under noisy conditions
InterpretiveSynthesis: Multimodal resources are promising but narrower and harder to evaluate than audio-only corpora
ResidualRisk: AVSR evidence may be language and domain concentrated
WritingUse: Frame AVSR as future agenda evidence

Definition: Within-language acoustic lexical and phonological variation across speaker communities
EstablishedEvidence: Inclusive benchmark and fairness evidence show aggregate language scores can hide subgroup failures
InterpretiveSynthesis: Dialect variation makes low-resource status a coverage and evaluation problem
ResidualRisk: Metadata may be missing or inconsistent

Definition: Multiple accepted spellings formatting conventions diacritics spacing and punctuation practices
EstablishedEvidence: Data-quality and lenient-evaluation evidence show transcript conventions change measured errors
InterpretiveSynthesis: Orthography should be treated as a resource and evaluation variable
ResidualRisk: Some normalization evidence is language-specific

Definition: Utterances containing multiple languages or scripts in one speech event
EstablishedEvidence: Existing matrices flag code-switching as an adaptation and evaluation risk
InterpretiveSynthesis: Code-switching stresses tokenization language modeling and constrained correction
ResidualRisk: Direct Core 60 ASR evidence is thinner than general multilingual evidence
WritingUse: Use as caution in language condition and future agenda

Definition: Large surface-form variation from inflection derivation or compounding
EstablishedEvidence: Morphology interacts with WER CER and tokenization choices
InterpretiveSynthesis: Metric interpretation must consider language structure and segmentation
ResidualRisk: Needs more language-specific evidence before strong claims

Definition: Non-Latin scripts multiple scripts optional marks spacing and text-normalization complexity
EstablishedEvidence: Multilingual benchmark evidence and lenient scoring show script effects matter
InterpretiveSynthesis: Script complexity links resource preparation to fair comparison
ResidualRisk: Do not imply one universal normalization rule
WritingUse: Use in taxonomy and metric critique

Definition: Transfer difficulty caused by typological phonetic or orthographic distance from pretraining languages
EstablishedEvidence: Multilingual SSL and low-resource SFM evaluation show transfer gains are uneven
InterpretiveSynthesis: Foundation-model benefit depends on language relatedness and coverage
ResidualRisk: Family-level claims need careful benchmark support

Definition: Traditional ASR pipelines with acoustic language and pronunciation components
EstablishedEvidence: Low-resource ASR surveys and Babel work document pre-foundation constraints
InterpretiveSynthesis: Hybrid ASR provides historical baseline for resource and lexicon bottlenecks
ResidualRisk: Risk of overlong history

Definition: Neural systems trained to map speech to token sequences with reduced pipeline modularity
EstablishedEvidence: Survey and self-training evidence show E2E systems shifted data and supervision needs
InterpretiveSynthesis: E2E simplifies pipelines but can raise labeled-data and regularization demands
ResidualRisk: Do not make it a method-by-method survey

Definition: Self-supervised pretrained acoustic encoders such as wav2vec 2.0 HuBERT WavLM and related models
EstablishedEvidence: SSL models are central foundation-era evidence
InterpretiveSynthesis: SSL reduces dependence on labeled data while leaving adaptation and evaluation bottlenecks
ResidualRisk: Some entries are verified-secondary and need careful wording

Definition: SSL systems pretrained across many languages for cross-lingual transfer
EstablishedEvidence: Multilingual SSL and MMS show scaling language coverage helps but unevenly
InterpretiveSynthesis: Multilinguality is a transfer condition not a guarantee of reliability
ResidualRisk: Aggregate results may hide language-family failures

Definition: Large pretrained ASR systems trained with weak labels at scale
EstablishedEvidence: Whisper MMS and OpusLM show major capability gains
InterpretiveSynthesis: Weakly supervised foundation models shift bottlenecks toward validation correction and evaluation
ResidualRisk: Do not claim solved low-resource ASR

Definition: Models integrating speech encoders with language-model style generation or reasoning
EstablishedEvidence: SpeechLM evidence is growing and hallucination evidence warns about generation risks
InterpretiveSynthesis: SpeechLMs are future-facing for ASR but require constrained evaluation
ResidualRisk: Many sources are emerging or not pure ASR

Definition: Systems that combine speech text translation and sometimes ASR across modalities
EstablishedEvidence: Speech-text and AVSR systems show expanding model scope
InterpretiveSynthesis: Multimodal foundation models support robustness agenda but ASR claims must stay bounded
ResidualRisk: Translation-centric systems are not standalone ASR evidence

Definition: Updating all model parameters on target language or domain data
EstablishedEvidence: Full fine-tuning remains common and effective in many settings
InterpretiveSynthesis: It can be expensive and susceptible to overfitting or forgetting
ResidualRisk: Comparisons often omit matched compute budgets

Definition: Additional SSL or foundation-model pretraining on target or related speech before supervised adaptation
EstablishedEvidence: Recent ASR studies test continued pretraining for target fit
InterpretiveSynthesis: Continued pretraining is useful when unlabeled target or related speech exists
ResidualRisk: Results depend on data similarity and budget

Definition: Adding or tuning small adapter modules for efficient domain or language adaptation
EstablishedEvidence: Adapters have strong method anchors and emerging ASR-specific evidence
InterpretiveSynthesis: Adapters are promising for low-resource compute constraints but direct evidence is uneven
ResidualRisk: Do not overgeneralize NLP results to ASR

Definition: Low-rank or quantized parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods
EstablishedEvidence: LoRA and QLoRA provide strong efficiency method anchors
InterpretiveSynthesis: They motivate ASR PEFT but require ASR-specific validation
ResidualRisk: Core evidence is method anchor more than ASR proof

Definition: Using prompts contexts or biasing information to guide ASR or speech-language models
EstablishedEvidence: Local matrices treat prompting and contextual ASR as emerging
InterpretiveSynthesis: Prompting can help but introduces leakage over-correction and hallucination risks
ResidualRisk: Watchlist evidence cannot support strong central claims

Definition: Using pretrained related-language or multilingual models for target-language ASR
EstablishedEvidence: Transfer is the core foundation-era adaptation mechanism
InterpretiveSynthesis: Effectiveness depends on language relatedness domain match and target data
ResidualRisk: Aggregate transfer results can hide poor target languages

Definition: Preventing loss of existing multilingual capability while adding a new language or domain
EstablishedEvidence: Recent ASR work directly addresses adding a language without forgetting
InterpretiveSynthesis: Forgetting control turns adaptation into a multi-objective problem
ResidualRisk: Evidence base is still small

Definition: Training or adapting with human-verified paired speech and text
EstablishedEvidence: Supervised data remains necessary for calibration and evaluation
InterpretiveSynthesis: Foundation models reduce but do not remove need for verified supervision
ResidualRisk: Labeled datasets may be narrow or poorly documented

Definition: Learning speech representations from unlabeled audio
EstablishedEvidence: SSL is a major technical shift in low-resource ASR
InterpretiveSynthesis: SSL changes pretraining assumptions but not final validation needs
ResidualRisk: Some model papers are not low-resource-specific

Definition: Iterative training with model-generated labels
EstablishedEvidence: Self-training and noisy student evidence support supervision expansion
InterpretiveSynthesis: Self-training works only when label quality and domain match are controlled
ResidualRisk: Teacher error propagation remains a core risk

Definition: Selecting pseudo-labels by confidence uncertainty calibration or multi-stage filters
EstablishedEvidence: Filtering evidence makes reliability central rather than optional
InterpretiveSynthesis: Filtering is the bridge between data-centric and supervision-centric strategy
ResidualRisk: Filtering rules are often not comparable

Definition: Using one teacher model to train or compress a student ASR model
EstablishedEvidence: KD can transfer knowledge and support compression
InterpretiveSynthesis: Single-teacher KD depends heavily on teacher errors and target mismatch
ResidualRisk: Need distinguish KD levels and objectives

Definition: Learning from multiple teachers or multilingual teacher ensembles
EstablishedEvidence: Multi-teacher evidence suggests coverage benefits
InterpretiveSynthesis: Teacher disagreement becomes a selection and reliability problem
ResidualRisk: Disagreement reporting remains thin

Definition: Selecting labels or teachers based on agreement disagreement or reliability estimates
EstablishedEvidence: Local evidence flags teacher agreement as important but underdeveloped
InterpretiveSynthesis: Agreement selection should be a future reproducibility requirement
ResidualRisk: Direct evidence is limited and should be phrased as agenda

Definition: Standard word or character error rate reporting
EstablishedEvidence: WER and CER remain necessary metrics
InterpretiveSynthesis: They are insufficient without language-aware normalization and subgroup reporting
ResidualRisk: Do not reject standard metrics outright

Definition: Scoring that accounts for spelling variation formatting diacritics script and normalization
EstablishedEvidence: Lenient scoring and data-quality evidence show orthography affects comparability
InterpretiveSynthesis: Evaluation must document transcript normalization and scoring scripts
ResidualRisk: Language-specific rules may not generalize

Definition: Reporting performance by dialect variety accent or speaker community
EstablishedEvidence: Dialect and fairness evidence warn against pooled scores
InterpretiveSynthesis: Dialect-wise reporting is central for reliable low-resource ASR
ResidualRisk: Metadata can be incomplete or sensitive

Definition: Reporting performance by recording condition speech style channel or deployment domain
EstablishedEvidence: Challenge and robustness evidence show domain and channel mismatch matters
InterpretiveSynthesis: Domain-wise reporting links resources to deployment validity
ResidualRisk: Not all datasets include comparable domains

Definition: Testing performance under noise reverberation distance overlap and meetings
EstablishedEvidence: CHiME and AVSR sources support robustness beyond clean speech
InterpretiveSynthesis: Robustness should be treated as evaluation not optional stress testing
ResidualRisk: Some robust benchmarks are not low-resource-specific

Definition: Testing disparities by accent race gender age provenance or demographic metadata
EstablishedEvidence: Fairness studies show aggregate ASR performance can hide disparities
InterpretiveSynthesis: Low-resource evaluation should report metadata-aware subgroup results where ethical and available
ResidualRisk: Demographic categories must be handled carefully

Definition: Ability to reproduce scores through data splits recipes code model versions and decoding settings
EstablishedEvidence: Toolkits and benchmarks support reproducible ASR practice
InterpretiveSynthesis: Reproducibility is part of evidence quality not just engineering
ResidualRisk: Toolkit existence is not proof of reproducible papers

Definition: Reporting training adaptation inference memory and deployment constraints
EstablishedEvidence: PEFT and SUPERB efficiency evidence support cost-aware evaluation
InterpretiveSynthesis: Compute reporting determines whether methods are realistic for under-resourced settings
ResidualRisk: Compute evidence may rely on non-ASR method anchors

Definition: Evaluating audio-visual recognition under noisy or degraded audio conditions
EstablishedEvidence: AV-HuBERT robust AVSR and MuAViC support multimodal robustness
InterpretiveSynthesis: AVSR is promising for noisy settings but resource coverage is narrow
ResidualRisk: Multilingual and multidialect AVSR evidence is limited
WritingUse: Use in Section 11 and future agenda

Definition: Testing fabricated content semantic drift and unconstrained correction in ASR or LLM-assisted ASR
EstablishedEvidence: Careless Whisper plus watchlist sources show WER can miss harmful failure modes
InterpretiveSynthesis: Hallucination and over-correction require constrained evaluation beyond average WER
ResidualRisk: Most current LLM-related evidence is emerging
WritingUse: Use with caution in future-facing claims

Definition: Evaluating LLM correction rescoring contextual ASR and post-ASR normalization with constraints
EstablishedEvidence: Local watchlist identifies concrete LLM-assisted ASR evaluation risks
InterpretiveSynthesis: LLM assistance should be framed as constrained correction or rescoring rather than free rewriting
ResidualRisk: Watchlist-only sources cannot carry central claims
